title: Combating the Memory Walls: Optimization Pathways for Long-Context Agentic LLM Inference
evidence_span: PLENA targets long-context agentic LLM inference, where large DOMs and tool-call trajectories create bandwidth and capacity memory walls. It combines hardware supporting asymmetric quantization, a flattened systolic array with native FlashAttention support, and a full stack with custom ISA, compiler, cycle-emulated simulator, and automated design-space exploration. Simulated results report up to 8.5x higher utilization than existing accelerators, 2.24x higher throughput than an A100, and 3.85x higher throughput than a TPU v6e under matched multiplier and memory settings; the system is intended for open-source release.
problem: Long-context agentic LLM inference generates large off-chip memory traffic from extended web, tool, and interaction histories, creating simultaneous bandwidth and capacity memory walls that leave compute units underutilized.
method_or_artifact: PLENA hardware-software co-design with asymmetric-quantization compute/memory units, a flattened FlashAttention-capable systolic array, custom ISA, compiler, cycle-emulated simulator, and automated design-space exploration flow.
workload_or_benchmark: Long-context agentic LLM inference involving web or computer-use inputs, tool-call trajectories, and extended contexts; evaluation uses simulated accelerator execution and matched multiplier/memory settings against A100 and TPU v6e references.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Custom accelerator with flattened systolic array, asymmetric quantization, custom ISA/compiler, and cycle-emulated simulation; reported gains are simulated and depend on matched hardware-resource assumptions.
metrics: up to 8.5x higher utilization than existing accelerators
2.24x throughput over A100 under matched settings
3.85x throughput over TPU v6e under matched settings
custom ISA, compiler, simulator, and DSE stack
limits: The evidence is an author preprint abstract and simulated evaluation; exact models, context lengths, memory hierarchy, area/energy, simulator validation, and the status of open-source artifacts require full-paper verification.

title: Approaching Shannon Bound with Lossless LLM Weight Compression
evidence_span: The study analyzes LLM weight entropy from 1.5B to 405B parameter models across bf16, int4, AWQ, and SQ8 formats, finding effective entropy 2–10x lower than stored bitwidth and theoretical footprint reduction up to 10x without changing weight values. It introduces tile-level on-the-fly lossless decompression using Asymmetric Numeral Systems aligned with GPU GEMM tiling. The system reaches within 0.01–0.1 bits of the Shannon limit, raises Qwen-14B maximum batch size from 47 to 75, improves Mixtral-176B batch size from 20 to 95, and reports up to 1.2x/1.6x throughput gains plus up to 11x over NeuZip and DFloat11.
problem: Trillion-parameter LLM weights can exceed GPU memory capacity, while conventional stored bitwidth overstates the intrinsic randomness of weights and lossless compression has not been tightly integrated with inference execution.
method_or_artifact: Entropy analysis across model sizes and numeric formats, followed by tile-level Asymmetric Numeral Systems compression and on-the-fly decompression aligned to GPU GEMM tiling, integrated with SGLang and multi-GPU serving.
workload_or_benchmark: LLM serving across 1.5B–405B parameter models and bf16/int4/AWQ/SQ8 formats, including Qwen-14B and Mixtral-176B batch-size and throughput evaluation; comparisons include NeuZip and DFloat11.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: GPU inference with tile-level decompression integrated into SGLang and multi-GPU serving; exact decompression hardware/software cost, memory bandwidth, GPU models, and quality invariance conditions require full-paper verification.
metrics: up to 11x throughput improvement over NeuZip and DFloat11
limits: The evidence is an author preprint abstract; exact compression/decompression latency, CPU/GPU overhead, memory-bandwidth accounting, model-quality invariance, sequence lengths, and hardware implementation details require full-paper verification.
